claims_about_writeup.quote: `contribution.md` says all of this plainly, with my estimate of where it sits on your novelty axis.
claims_about_writeup.why: The write-up has a section explicitly titled 'Relation to prior work, stated plainly' listing the four concrete differences from Raman 2026, plus a 'What is new, and what it shows' section giving an explicit reading of the method's novelty ('a sharp functional point', 'a strong constraint on where such a property can live'), matching the claim.

message_source_quote: it's the **white-bear (think vs don't-think) stance direction** — the method of `raman2026-white-bear-steering.md` (which is in `papers/` and whose setup is exactly this task: same model, same read layers, their 0.14 baseline ≈ our 0.1275)
writeup_source_quote: This is the same method family as white-bear steering (Raman, Wierzbicki & Fournier 2026, `papers/raman2026-white-bear-steering.md`): a concept-agnostic stance contrast, a large dose over a mid-depth band, an effect that is *computed* by the layers above the band rather than read back from the vector.

differences.what: caveat that the single-cell direction estimate is noisier than the paper's carrier-average estimate, which affects how well the reproduction matches the source's quality
differences.message_quote: the direction is **re-estimated from our own DM dev bank** (53 pairs pooled fit+val, carrier-final cell — the paper's 35 bench pairs unused; estimates agree to cos 0.994)
differences.writeup_quote: its leave-one-pair-out cosine is 0.57-0.61 vs ≥0.997 for the carrier average; the estimate is noisier, which matters for the dose below)

rationale: Both documents explicitly name and credit Raman 2026 as the method the submission reproduces/builds on, give the same list of four differences (re-estimated direction, single-cell vs carrier-average read, bank-dependent dose peak at 4.2 vs the paper's 6, load-bearing 5-layer band), and frame the novelty identically as a systematic mapping of the functional basin rather than a new contrast. The message adds an extra point of overlap not stated in the write-up (same model/read-layers setup and a matching ~0.14 vs 0.1275 baseline) while omitting the write-up's caveat that the single-cell estimate is noisier than the paper's carrier-token average.
